title: Follow the pack/profile/qualification anatomy and naming
summary: The Sphere Editor owns the canonical new layout. Authors should request templates and bounded mutations rather than memorising filenames. Legacy layouts remain readable; new/editor-managed writes use the canonical packs/<sphere>/{articles,corpora,rules,services,languages} structure plus profile/tests/qualification/changelog.

anatomy.packs_&_profile: packs/<id>/NN.json objects plus profiles/<id>.json; profile lists ['packs/core','packs/<id>'] unless engine services (packs/core or packs/oorexx) are needed.
anatomy.object_kinds: sphere (manifest), access-policy, article, corpus, service, language-rule
anatomy.human_entry: a top <ID>_SPHERE.md, plus tests/run_<id>.sh and qualification/QUALIFICATION.txt + MANIFEST.sha256
anatomy.versioning: bump the sphere/prod object's version for a material change (e.g. a doctrinal fix), do not silently reshape an id

evidence_note: accounting-rigour, llm-containment, python-best-practices and bash-best-practices all share this shape and were loadable via `sphere resolve/load` and had zero (kind,id) collisions.
invariants: Use unique (kind,id) pairs and let the editor choose canonical paths.
Use the profile to compose core/shared packs and the sphere pack.
Ship an access policy appropriate to the intended readers/operators.
Do not destructively rearrange a qualified legacy sphere merely for cosmetic conformity.
